subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a bundled Slack-plugin `assistant.search.context` action, and what token lifetime, privacy, scope, and user-consent contract should govern event-scoped Slack `action_token`s?
rationale: The missing behavior is a new workspace-search capability that crosses auth-provider, search visibility, and secret-handling boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API shape or retention model.

options.title: Add narrow RTS support
options.body: Implement a Slack-owned read-only RTS action that keeps action tokens ephemeral, redacted, thread/account-bound, and proven in a live Slack workspace.

options.title: Defer to external plugin
options.body: Leave bundled Slack unchanged until maintainers want to own the RTS security contract, allowing experimentation outside core/plugin distribution first.

options.title: Revive legacy message search
options.body: Use `search.messages` user-token search instead, accepting that it is not the requested Slack RTS API and needs separate privacy/authorization review.

recommendation.title: Add narrow RTS support
recommendation.body: Implement a Slack-owned read-only RTS action that keeps action tokens ephemeral, redacted, thread/account-bound, and proven in a live Slack workspace.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across Slack assistant lifecycle, action runtime, and the PR close decision that routed search back to this issue.
